headline: Court Leaves Duterte Trial to Senate
deck: The Supreme Court dismissed two challenges as moot after the House transmitted the impeachment articles against Vice President Sara Duterte. The Senate, already convened as an impeachment court, is now the venue for trial.
body: The Philippine Supreme Court dismissed two challenges to the House impeachment process against Vice President Sara Duterte after the articles had already been transmitted to the Senate [E1]. The cases were docketed as G.R. E-05546 and E-05667 [E1]. The court declared them moot because the House action they sought to challenge had already advanced beyond the House [E1].

Transmission changed where the constitutional proceeding now sits [E1]. The House phase is complete, and the Senate had already convened as an impeachment court to receive the case [E2]. The trial therefore proceeds in the Senate, which is now the venue for adjudicating the articles [E2][E3].

Mootness also sets the boundary of what the court decided [E1]. The PIO statement reports a procedural dismissal, with no finding that Duterte is guilty or innocent [E1]. It supplies no basis for predicting conviction, acquittal or any other Senate outcome [E1][E2].

With the House phase closed, the petitions can no longer stop or redo the transmission described in the official statement [E1]. The dismissal removes the remaining challenge directed at the House process [E3]. Independent Philippine coverage likewise places the next consequential proceeding before the Senate impeachment court [E2][E4].

That narrow act still carries institutional weight because it clears a live procedural obstacle from the case [E3]. The justices did not take over the Senate’s trial function or settle the allegations contained in the articles [E1][E2]. Their action leaves the impeachment proceeding where the House’s transmission placed it: before the Senate [E1][E3].

One limitation remains material at publication: the full resolution PDF was unavailable, leaving the Supreme Court PIO statement as the primary artifact for the dismissal [E1]. The available record supports the stated ground of mootness and the procedural consequence of Senate proceedings [E1][E2]. It does not support claims about wider reasoning, separate doctrinal holdings or the justices’ treatment of arguments not described in that statement [E1].

The sequence is now plain: the House transmitted the articles, and the Supreme Court dismissed the two House-process challenges as moot [E1]. The Senate had already convened as an impeachment court, and the trial remains there [E2][E3]. The House contest is over; Duterte’s liability remains entirely undecided [E1][E2].

evidence_box.fragment: G.R. E-05546 and E-05667 were moot after House transmission to the Senate.
Proceedings moved to a Senate already convened as an impeachment court.
The dismissal removes the House-process challenge and leaves the Senate trial proceeding.
Independent coverage corroborated the dismissal and its consequence for the Senate.
